answer: Earn a canyon-crossing passport by climbing a spiral of twelve tasks, each stamped by a different plume verifier. Registration binds a hardware key and locks a 50 POA deposit; verifiers are drawn at random and paid from forfeited deposits. Finishing all twelve steps in fourteen days earns the passport, and any failed step burns the deposit. Forging 100 passports costs 5,000 POA in deposits, 3,600 POA in fees, and 1,200 hours of work. Like a canyon crossing where each climber plants a signed flag at every camp, one honest agent climbs cheaply and a fake army pays for a hundred ascents.
